evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/marketplace/ — the entire Epic 68 Service Provider Marketplace UI (6 pages: MarketplacePage, CreateRfqPage, ProviderDetailPage, ProviderProfilePage, QuoteComparisonPage, RfqListPage — see pages/index.ts barrel — plus ~14 components) is never mounted into the router. `grep -rn "features/marketplace" src --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts` returns ZERO references outside the feature directory, and none of the 6 page components are referenced in src/routes/** (CreateRfqPage/QuoteComparisonPage/RfqListPage/ProviderDetailPage/ProviderProfilePage → 0 route refs). src/routes/AppRoutes.tsx:38-68 composes 23 feature route-group fragments and NONE import features/marketplace; lazyRoutes.tsx has no marketplace entry. NOTE the trap: the only wired `MarketplacePage` is a DIFFERENT component, features/community/pages/MarketplacePage.tsx (community classifieds), exported at features/community/index.ts:32 and routed at routes/groups/community.tsx:254 as /community/marketplace — it is NOT the Epic 68 service-provider marketplace. Consequence: a fully-built, polished epic's UI is dead code — unreachable by users, invisible to route/screen-map coverage, and excluded from bundle route-splitting. Fix (frontend-only, cloud-landable): add a marketplaceRoutes() group under routes/groups/, wire the 6 pages to container route-wrappers (data hooks + API↔UI mappers) and register it in AppRoutes.tsx, or explicitly delete/park the feature if descoped. Medium: shipped feature functionally unreachable, no crash.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/ — the pet/vehicle Registry feature (RegistryPage, RegistryRulesPage + forms/lists/modal components) is imported nowhere outside its own directory: `grep -rn "features/registry" src` returns zero external refs, no registryRoutes() group exists, and src/routes/AppRoutes.tsx:38-68 registers no registry group. Yet RegistryPage's own handlers navigate via hard `window.location.href = '/registry/pets/new'` / '/registry/vehicles/{id}/edit' (RegistryPage.tsx:91,95,129,148,152,186) — routes that are never registered, so every such navigation lands on the NotFound/error route. The feature is therefore both unreachable (no entry route) and internally broken (its nav targets 404). Fix (frontend-only, cloud-landable): add a registryRoutes() group wiring RegistryPage + RegistryRulesPage (and the pet/vehicle detail/edit/new sub-routes the handlers already point at) and register it in AppRoutes.tsx; prefer react-router useNavigate over window.location.href so the SPA doesn't full-reload. Medium: shipped feature unreachable + dead internal links, no crash.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx — all four destructive/approval mutations swallow failures with only console.error and give the user NO feedback: handlePetDelete (98-109), handlePetReview (111-126), handleVehicleDelete (155-166), handleVehicleReview (168-183) each do `try { await mutation.mutateAsync(...) } catch (error) { console.error(...) }`. On a failed delete or approval (403/409/network) the user sees the row unchanged and no error toast/banner, so they assume success (or retry blindly) — a classic silent-failure UX trap on a manager-facing moderation surface. Distinct from the existing code-review-ppt-web-ui-registry-rules-save-silent-fail finding, which is RegistryRulesPage (rules save), not these RegistryPage registration handlers. Fix (frontend-only, cloud-landable): surface mutation errors via the app toast/error system (and ideally use the mutation's onError + isError state), and add a Vitest case asserting a visible error is rendered when mutateAsync rejects. Medium: unhandled error on a user-facing action path, no crash.
